name: hcapp_sendKennelMessage
description: Posts a message to a KENNEL-level chat thread: an HC.EventMessage row with KennelId set and EventId NULL. Mirrors hcapp_sendEventMessage's three-rowset shape so the API shim's push dispatch is unchanged. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 64, @param NULL — a standard device-secret token). Permission gate: NONE — anyone authenticated may post in any kennel's chat (James, 2026-10-11, E9.F1.S30; the former follower/member refusal is gone). Posting joins the kennel's chat: a hasher with no HasherKennelMap row gets one (Following 0, MemberSince NULL, KennelNotificationPreference 1), and an existing row whose bell was never chosen (0) is turned on; explicit Off (2) / muted (3) / before-run (4) are never overridden, and a removed row is left alone. Who is PUSHED is unchanged and is drawn from HasherKennelMap: only hashers who chose a kennel bell (1, 3, 4), on live devices signed in within 180 days, on builds >= HC6.MinBuildForChatPush(), who have not blocked the sender, and who match the releasability bits. Rowset 0's MessageContent is HC6.ChatMessagePreview (the push body), not the raw content. Since 2026-10-13 a resend of an already-stored @messageId by the same sender in the same thread is idempotent: nothing is written, rowset 0 returns the stored message and the push rowsets are empty, so nobody is notified twice (a resend after a lost reply used to hit PK_EventMessage and report a delivered message as unsent). The post-commit part ran outside any TRY (a failure was an unlogged raw 500 for a stored message); it now has a TRY whose CATCH logs 'Push audience failed in sendKennelMessage' and swallows.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Default NULL (ValidateAppAuth then fails gracefully).

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token (standard, device secret; @param NULL). Default NULL.

parameters.name: kennelId
parameters.description: The kennel whose chat receives the message. Required; NULL → errorCode 1901.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: Client-generated message UUID. Required; NULL → errorCode 1901. A duplicate id is a PK violation caught by the CATCH (errorCode 1933) — the insert is not idempotent.

parameters.name: messageTitle
parameters.description: Optional title; NULL is stored as ''. Rowset 0 returns it prefixed with the sender's DisplayName + ' - '.

parameters.name: messageContent
parameters.description: Message body (text, a chat-photos blob URL, or a map link by @messageKind). Required; empty/NULL → 1901. More than 4,000 UTF-16 code units (the column width) is REFUSED with 1902 rather than truncated — the parameter is MAX for that reason.

parameters.name: messageReleasabilityFlags
parameters.description: Push-audience bitmask: 0x0001 mismanagement, 0x0002 members (MembershipExpirationDate in the future), 0x0004 followers, 0x0020 everyone. NULL → 63 (all). 0x0008 RSVPs and 0x0010 hares are stored but ignored here — a kennel thread has no run.

parameters.name: messageKind
parameters.description: 0 text (default), 1 photo, 2 location (E9.F1.S11/S12). NULL → 0. Validated by HC6.ChatMessageKindError; a bad kind/content pairing → 1903.

parameters.name: replyToMessageId
parameters.description: The message this one quotes (E9.F1.S21). Kept only when it is a message of THIS kennel thread (KennelId match, EventId NULL); otherwise silently cleared and the message sends without a quote.

rowsets.description: Returned alone, then RETURN, on: auth failure (codes/types from ValidateAppAuth); 1901 missing messageId/kennelId/content (errorType 2); 1902 content over 4,000 (2); 1903 bad message kind (2); 1933 unhandled error in the write transaction (5). The push-audience queries after the commit are NOT inside a TRY, so a failure there is a raw HTTP 500 after rowset 0 has been sent.

rowsets.name: InsertedMessage
rowsets.description: On success: the just-inserted message, one row, for the sender's optimistic UI and the API's push body.

columns.name: PublicKennelId
columns.description: EventMessage.PublicKennelId, copied from Kennel.PublicKennelId at insert.

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: Hasher.PublicHasherId of the sender (not the internal id).

columns.name: MessageTitle
columns.description: DisplayName + ' - ' + EventMessage.MessageTitle ('' when none was given).

columns.name: MessageContent
columns.description: HC6.ChatMessagePreview(MessageKind, MessageContent): the text, or a photo/location placeholder. The API uses it as the push body — it is NOT the raw stored content for a photo or location.

columns.name: MessageReleasabilityFlags
columns.description: EventMessage.MessageReleasabilityFlags as stored (63 when the caller passed NULL).

columns.name: EventChatMessageCount
columns.description: Always 0 — kept for shape parity with hcapp_sendEventMessage.

columns.name: MessageType
columns.description: EventMessage.MessageType — 0 for a kennel thread (non-zero values name a global room).

columns.name: KennelShortName
columns.description: Kennel.KennelShortName, so the phone can title the thread a push opens. Added 2026-09-18.

rowsets.name: VisiblePushRecipients
rowsets.description: On success: one row per distinct FCM token whose hasher's KennelNotificationPreference is 1 (on) or 4 (on before the run — treated as on, a kennel thread has no run window). Audience: HasherKennelMap rows for @kennelId, not removed, hasher not removed, device not removed with a token and LastLogin within 180 days, build >= HC6.MinBuildForChatPush() (TRY_CAST — '<unknown>' fails closed), not blocking the sender (HasherFriendMap.Ignore), and matching the releasability bits. The sender's own devices are included on purpose (the echo drives the delivered tick). May be empty.

columns.name: BadgeTotal
columns.description: HC6.UserUnreadChatTotal for the recipient — the app-icon badge the API puts in aps.badge / notification_count. NULL when no device with that token is on a build >= HC6.MinBuildForIconBadge() (older apps never lower the icon).

rowsets.name: SilentPushRecipients
rowsets.description: On success: the same audience with KennelNotificationPreference 3 (on but muted) — a data-only push so the badge moves without a notification. Same columns as rowset 1. May be empty.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.EventMessage (KennelId set, EventId NULL) — fires HC.trgCreateSeqNum (assigns MessageSequenceCount) and HC.trgEventMessageActivityCount (no-op for a kennel thread: EventId is NULL).

INSERT HC.HasherKennelMap (UserId, KennelId, Following 0, MemberSince NULL, KennelNotificationPreference 1) when the sender has no row for the kennel (existence check WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK) ignores `removed`, so a removed row is never revived); else UPDATE KennelNotificationPreference 0 → 1 on a live row (2/3/4 untouched). The kennel bell also governs that kennel's RSVP and check-in reminders.
MERGE HC.EventMessageBadgeCounts (UserId, KennelId) — the sender's last-read position moves to the new MessageSequenceCount so they never see their own message as unread.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on every refused path and in the CATCH.
The API shim fans out FCM pushes from rowsets 1 and 2 (visible / silent); nothing is queued in the database.

codeSmells.detail: Line 118 reads Kennel.PublicKennelId into a variable; an unknown @kennelId leaves it NULL and the INSERT at line 154 then fails on FK_EventMessage_Kennel inside the TRY → 1933 rather than a specific 'no such kennel' refusal. Also a HasherKennelMap row would be attempted first (line 145–148) and fail on its own FK. Harmless in practice (the app only sends ids it synced) but the error is misreported.

Lines 192–195 decode only mismanagement/members/followers/everyone. A caller passing only RSVPs (0x0008) or hares (0x0010) gets a message stored with those bits and NO push audience at all, with no refusal. hcapp_sendEventMessage rejects a mask with no usable bit (its line 119–121); here a NULL mask becomes 63 but a non-zero useless mask is accepted.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
